'''Barbara L. Osofsky''' (born August 4, 1937)<ref>Birth year from [http://d-nb.info/gnd/138868778 German National Library catalog entry], retrieved 2018-11-30.</ref> is a retired professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]].<ref>[http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~osofsky/ Barbara L. Osofsky]</ref> Her research concerns [[abstract algebra]].  Osofsky's contributions to mathematics include her characterization of [[Semisimple module#Semisimple rings|semisimple rings]] in terms of properties of [[cyclic module]]s.<ref name="HomologicalProperties">B. L. Osofsky, ''Homological properties of rings and modules'' (Doctoral dissertation, Rutgers University, 1964).</ref><ref name="LamCitationHomologicalProperties">[[T. Y. Lam]], ''Lectures on Modules and Rings''
Graduate Texts in Mathematics, 189 (Springer-Verlag, New York, 1999), p. 224.</ref>  Osofsky also established a [[logical equivalence]] between the [[continuum hypothesis]] and statements about the [[global dimension]] of [[Ring (mathematics)|associative rings]].<ref name="CHGlobalDim1">B. L. Osofsky, ''Homological dimension and the continuum hypothesis'',
Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. '''132''' (1968) 217–230.</ref><ref name="CHGlobalDim2">B. L. Osofsky, ''Homological dimension and cardinality'', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. '''151''' (1970) 641–649.</ref>

==Career==
Osofsky received her Ph.D. from Rutgers University in 1964.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=5678|title=Barbara Osofsky}}</ref> She then worked at Rutgers until 2004, when she retired.<ref name=newsletter/> She served as acting chair of the Rutgers mathematics department in 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/history.php|title=A History of Mathematics at Rutgers|author=[[Charles Weibel]]|access-date=Feb 1, 2015}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 1973, Osofsky addressed a national meeting of the AMS. She was the first woman in 50 years to do so. She became the first female editor of an AMS journal in 1974 when she became the editor of [[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]].<ref>Peter L. Duren, Richard Askey, [[Uta Merzbach|Uta C. Merzbach]] (1989) ''A Century of Mathematics in America'' American Mathematical Soc., p. 395</ref>

From 2000 to 2002, Osofsky served as First Vice-President of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=newsletter>{{cite web|title=Spring 2005 Newsletter|location=Rutgers Mathematics Department|url=http://www.math.rutgers.edu/newsletter/newsletter2005.html|access-date=Feb 1, 2015}}</ref> In 2005, she was awarded the MAA meritorious service award.

In 2012, Osofsky became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>

==Selected publications==
*  Osofsky, B. L. A generalization of quasi-Frobenius rings. ''J. Algebra'' 4 1966 373–387.
*Osofsky, B. L. Rings all of whose finitely generated modules are injective. ''Pacific J. Math.'' 14 1964 645–650.
*Osofsky, Barbara L.; Smith, Patrick F. Cyclic modules whose quotients have all complement submodules direct summands. ''J. Algebra'' 139 (1991), no. 2, 342–354.
